body:
# Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED

- FAIL AC-1: The run records BB environment, host and checkout, but continuation can throw after native dispatch while resolving its environment.
- FAIL AC-2: Status and ownership come from separate reads; a changed selection may display until the asynchronous ownership check completes.
- FAIL AC-3: Refresh occurs only while the panel is mounted; no host watch or server-side reconciliation updates closed panels or handles reconnect promptly.
- PASS AC-4: Native progress remains separate, and Open session targets the linked BB thread.
- FAIL AC-5: Merged-but-unclosed detection arrives asynchronously and may remain stale while the panel displays verified completion.
- FAIL AC-6: The host response contains no root or environment identity to validate, and duplicate-owner roots are not displayed.
- PASS AC-7: An isolated runnable UI fixture and browser assertions cover Start task, phase changes, input, blocked, offline/reconnect and completion; reviewer did not execute it.

## Security / correctness

No direct authentication bypass is evident in the committed diff. The main correctness gaps are unvalidated host observation identity, asynchronous status/ownership disagreement and a post-dispatch failure path.

## Design / maintainability

The implementation uses a host shell command and module-global ownership cache although accepted D-001 selects the read-only Empirical overview export. Separate status and ownership reads weaken the single-checkout snapshot.

findings.summary: The host returns only status, so the server stamps expected host and checkout onto a response without validating the actual source root.
Observations refresh only in mounted progress views; no journal watcher or server reconciliation updates closed panels or handles reconnect promptly.
Background ownership reads and a 30-second cache allow changed selection or merged-but-unclosed state to appear as current completion.
Continuation awaits environments.get after native dispatch without a catch, so lookup failure can prevent the dispatched run from being persisted.
Invalid and uninitialized observations overwrite the persisted last usable snapshot.
Duplicate-owner warning does not identify either claiming checkout root.
Host observation shells out to an executable on PATH, diverging from the accepted read-only Empirical export.
